description: We are a two-member team of Software Engineering students passionate about Artificial Intelligence, data-driven applications, web development, and space technology. We enjoy transforming complex problems and scientific data into practical, interactive software experiences.
summary:
FLAME is an AI-powered scientific research platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms complex NASA microgravity combustion data into understandable, interactive, and actionable scientific insights.
Fire behaves differently in microgravity, creating major challenges for spacecraft safety. FLAME addresses this by combining NASA experimental datasets, scientific visualizations, predictive data analysis, research gap detection, and AI-powered assistance in one platform.
The platform features an interactive fire simulation that demonstrates how environmental conditions, such as oxygen levels, influence flame behavior. Its Gemini AI-powered research assistant uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide evidence-based answers from scientific data and documents.
FLAME also supports experiment comparisons, fire safety research, Earth-based applications, and importing new datasets for future knowledge expansion.
Our mission is to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, accelerate scientific discovery, and contribute to safer space exploration.
details:
FLAME is an AI-powered research intelligence platform developed for the challenge "Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data."

Fire behaves differently in microgravity, creating unique risks for astronauts during future space missions. FLAME addresses the difficulty of finding, understanding and comparing NASA's extensive combustion research.

The platform integrates NASA research resources, including Saffire I–III, BASS/BASS-II, alongside historical spacecraft fire reports and technical publications.

Its AI research assistant provides evidence-grounded answers with supporting references. Additional features include a Dataset Explorer for visualizing experimental telemetry, Experiment Comparison, Predictive Modeling Data Extraction, Research Gap Detection, Fire Safety Equipment Research and Earth Applications.

FLAME combines scientific literature, experimental data and interactive analysis in one workspace. It helps researchers explore findings, compare experiments, prepare datasets for further analysis and identify gaps in existing research.

The platform was developed using React, JavaScript, Vite and Python with FastAPI, alongside Gemini API integration. Its goal is to make NASA combustion research more accessible and support safer human space exploration and improved fire safety on Earth.
